candidates.definition: A generic information-processing resource, such as a virtual machine or container, with configurable processor, memory, hostname, and lifecycle state.
candidates.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3.1, pp. 5-6, especially the opening paragraph and Tables 3-4
candidates.scopeRationale: This is OCCI's VM-capable execution resource and is central to the bounded VM-connected IaaS scope.

relations.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3.1, Table 4 and paragraph following it, p. 5

candidates.definition: An L2 interconnection resource, exemplified by a virtual switch, which can be extended with L3/L4 capabilities.
candidates.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3.2, pp. 6-7, especially the opening paragraph and Tables 5-6
candidates.scopeRationale: It represents the network to which a VM-capable Compute resource is explicitly connected.

candidates.definition: A mixin that adds an IP address range, gateway, and dynamic-or-static address allocation settings to a Network.
candidates.scopeRationale: It supplies the L3 addressing configuration for a network connected to Compute.

candidates.definition: A resource that records information on a data-storage device and exposes size and lifecycle state.
candidates.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3.3, p. 8, especially the opening paragraph and Tables 8-9
candidates.scopeRationale: It is the persistent-storage resource explicitly attachable to a VM-capable Compute resource.

candidates.definition: An L2 client-device link, such as a network adapter, used to connect a Compute instance to a Network instance.
candidates.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3 and Figure 1, p. 4; Section 3.4.1, p. 9, including Table 10
candidates.scopeRationale: This is the explicit VM-to-network attachment boundary rather than a standalone network resource.

candidates.definition: A mixin that adds an IP address, optional gateway, and dynamic-or-static allocation mechanism to a NetworkInterface.
candidates.scopeRationale: It captures per-interface L3 addressing on the explicit Compute-to-Network link.

candidates.definition: A link from a Resource to a target Storage instance that lets Storage be attached to Compute while the implementation handles prerequisite low-level operations.
candidates.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3.4.2, pp. 10-11, especially the opening paragraph and Table 12
candidates.scopeRationale: This is the explicit VM-to-storage attachment boundary and carries device and optional guest mount information.

relations.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3 and Figure 1, p. 4; Section 3.4.2, p. 10

candidates.definition: A provider-defined template mixin identifying a particular operating-system image configuration to install on a requested Compute resource.
candidates.scopeRationale: It represents the boot execution-environment choice for a VM-capable Compute resource.

relations.sourceLocator: GFD.224, Section 3.1, Table 4 and paragraph following it, p. 5

candidates.definition: A provider-defined template mixin representing a preset Resource configuration whose values override applicable size-related attributes on an associated Resource.
candidates.scopeRationale: Its Compute example captures preset VM sizing while retaining the document's broader Resource-level semantics.

candidates.definition: A Compute-only mixin that carries a client's public SSH key for provider-mediated injection when the Compute resource is created.
candidates.scopeRationale: It is a bounded VM provisioning input for SSH-secured access, not a general identity or secret-management catalog.

candidates.definition: A Compute-only mixin carrying one-time client contextualization data that is supplied during instantiation and executed at the end of the Compute boot order.
candidates.scopeRationale: It captures VM bootstrap configuration directly tied to Compute creation without expanding into application management.
